summary:
The sample implements the requested Python LangChain + Beanie agent: it reads submitted reports, applies an LLM (when OPENAI_API_KEY is present) or a deterministic fallback, applies session memory across a run, flags policy violations, and writes enriched reports back to Azure DocumentDB. The repo includes an idempotent seeder, index-creation script, .env.example, and a README. Key operational best-practice gaps remain (atomic idempotent processing, vector/index guidance left intentionally out, connection-pool tuning, tests that run offline, and an IaC example). See requirement_results and checks for line-level evidence and the smallest-fix recommendations to make the sample gallery-ready.

Notes about environment: the build used the provided live cluster and MCP tools according to the build report. The sample was executed in deterministic demo mode (no LLM key), and the AI path was not exercised in this run because OPENAI_API_KEY was not provided.

requirement_results.requirement: Implement the agent in Python with LangChain as a single agent that, for each submitted expense report, reads the report, categorises its line items, flags policy violations and writes the enriched report back.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/processor.py lines 85-106 (process_submitted_reports iterates Report.find, classifies items and saves updated report); app/src/processor.py lines 27-56 (conditional LangChain call and JSON parsing).

requirement_results.requirement: Define Beanie ODM Document models for expense reports and use Beanie to read the submitted expense reports from Azure DocumentDB.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/models.py lines 16-26 (Report Document model); app/src/db.py lines 18-19 (await init_beanie(...)); app/src/processor.py lines 88-90 (Report.find usage).

requirement_results.requirement: Each line item in a report receives a category from the LLM (e.g. OpenAI through LangChain) through an engineered prompt that supplies the company policy and the line item's details.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/processor.py lines 36-44 (SystemMessage contains policy prompt and HumanMessage contains item fields); lines 46-56 parse the LLM response JSON.

requirement_results.requirement: Flag policy violations: each line item that breaks the company policy is marked as a violation in the agent's output for the report.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/processor.py lines 50-54 (parse policy_violation and violation_reason from LLM response); app/src/processor.py lines 65-82 (fallback classifier sets policy_violation and reason).

requirement_results.requirement: Write the enriched report back to Azure DocumentDB through Beanie, with the category and violation flag for each line item attached to the report document.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/processor.py lines 95-104 (update report.items[...] and await report.save()).

requirement_results.requirement: Provide an agent memory component that lives for a session spanning multiple reports and records the categorisation decisions the agent makes.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/processor.py lines 9-18 (SessionMemory class) and line 86 (memory = SessionMemory()) used across the processing loop.

requirement_results.requirement: When categorising a line item, the agent consults the session memory and applies an earlier decision to a matching item, so the same kind of expense receives the same category across the reports processed in that session.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/processor.py lines 21-26 (classify_item consults memory.get and returns stored category) and line 61 (memory.set after classification).

requirement_results.requirement: The connection string and model credentials come from environment variables; none appear in the repository.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/db.py line 10 reads DOCUMENTDB_URI from environment; app/src/processor.py lines 27 and 57 check OPENAI_API_KEY; app/.env.example lists placeholders (line 2, line 4). No secrets are checked in.

requirement_results.requirement: A .env.example lists every setting with placeholder values.
requirement_results.evidence: app/.env.example lines 2-8 include DOCUMENTDB_URI, OPENAI_API_KEY, USE_AI, DOCUMENTDB_DB placeholders.

requirement_results.requirement: The vector index dimensions match the embedding model's output.
requirement_results.evidence: No vector indexes were created (app/README.md line 38 states 'No vector indexes or embeddings were created'); app/src/indexes.py creates only B-tree indexes.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Ask the builder (in the starter prompt) to pick an embedding model and expose EMBEDDING_MODEL and EMBEDDING_DIM env settings, or add a skill rule that must provision vector indexes only when EMBEDDING_DIM is defined.

requirement_results.requirement: The vector index parameters are chosen for the sample's data size, and the README says how to change them for a larger one.
requirement_results.evidence: app/README.md explicitly says vector indexes were not created (line 38); indexes.py only creates B-tree indexes (lines 10-12).
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add to the starter prompt or sample README a short 'Vectors & Indexes' section that documents EMBEDDING_MODEL, EMBEDDING_DIM and recommended index parameters and how to adjust them for larger datasets.

requirement_results.requirement: One database client is created and reused across requests.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/db.py lines 6 and 13-16 implement a module-level singleton _client and reuse it in init_db/get_client.

requirement_results.requirement: A seed script loads sample data and creates the index, and can be run twice without duplicating data.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/seed.py lines 35-60 perform idempotent upsert by report_id (find_one and update/insert). app/src/indexes.py lines 10-12 create indexes (create_index is idempotent).

requirement_results.requirement: /search returns a clear error for an empty query and when the embedding call fails.
requirement_results.evidence: No HTTP server or /search endpoint is implemented in the sample (no FastAPI/Flask app present).
requirement_results.smallest_fix: If a search API is desired, add a small web handler (e.g., FastAPI) with a /search route that returns 400 for empty queries and returns a clear error payload when embedding or vector-query calls fail.

requirement_results.requirement: Search results include the similarity score.
requirement_results.evidence: No search or embedding-based query code is implemented; app/src/indexes.py only creates B-tree indexes and processors do not call vector search.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add similarity score in the search result model and return it from the vector-query path; require the embedding model/dim setting before enabling this feature.

requirement_results.requirement: Dependencies are pinned in requirements.txt.
requirement_results.evidence: app/requirements.txt pins major/minor ranges (beanie>=1.19,<2, motor>=3.1,<4, pydantic>=1.10,<2, etc.) instead of exact micro-version pins (no ==micro.patch pins).
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Pin exact micro versions (==) in requirements.txt, or include a constraints file with exact tested versions and a short README note about tested pins.

requirement_results.requirement: Unit tests run without a live cluster.
requirement_results.evidence: No unit test files are present; no test harness or mocked-driver fixtures were included in the repo.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add unit tests that mock Motor/Beanie (e.g., use asynctest/pytest-asyncio with monkeypatch on AsyncIOMotorClient or use a local DocumentDB Gateway in CI), and document how to run them without a live cluster.

requirement_results.requirement: Infrastructure for the cluster is provided as code, using the Azure DocumentDB resource type.
requirement_results.evidence: No IaC files (Bicep/Terraform/ARM) are present in the repository; the run used an existing cluster per the run environment.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add a minimal Bicep or Terraform example that uses Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongoClusters (or link to the AVM module) with parameters for tier/storage and a short snippet in README showing how to customize.

requirement_results.requirement: The README covers what the sample shows, prerequisites, setup, run, and clean-up.
requirement_results.evidence: app/README.md includes sections 'What this sample shows', 'Prerequisites', 'Quick start' (setup/run), and 'Cleanup' (lines 1-41).

requirement_results.requirement: The sample uses the name "Azure DocumentDB" throughout, and no former or neighbouring product name.
requirement_results.evidence: app/README.md title and body use 'Azure DocumentDB' (line 1). app/.env.example uses a mongocluster host (mongocluster.cosmos.azure.com) which is appropriate for the service.

checks.practice: Read the DocumentDB MongoDB-compatible connection string from an environment variable (e.g., DOCUMENTDB_URI) at runtime and do not check it into source control or logs.
checks.evidence: app/src/db.py line 10 reads DOCUMENTDB_URI; app/.env.example line 2 shows a placeholder SRV URI.

checks.practice: Create one MongoClient/driver client and reuse it (process-wide singleton).
checks.evidence: app/src/db.py lines 13-16 create and reuse a module-level AsyncIOMotorClient singleton (_client).

checks.practice: Always connect with TLS enabled and do not disable certificate validation in production.
checks.evidence: app/.env.example line 2 includes tls=true in the example URI; the client uses that URI (app/src/db.py line 15).

checks.practice: Use least-privilege credentials for applications (per-app users or Microsoft Entra ID + RBAC).
checks.evidence: The repo contains a placeholder DOCUMENTDB_URI (.env.example line 2) but does not create or document a least-privilege DB user; runtime credentials are external.
checks.what_would_help: A short README section or sample script that shows creating/using a readWrite user for sample_fintech_10, or an example of using MONGODB-OIDC/managed identity.

checks.practice: Include a schema or classifier version (and model identifier/dimensions where vectors are used).
checks.evidence: app/src/models.py line 21 defines schema_version on the Report document. No vector/model fields exist because vectors were not created.

checks.practice: Embed small, bounded arrays inside the parent document when children are always read together.
checks.evidence: app/src/models.py line 20 stores items: List[Item] on the Report document (embedded array).

checks.practice: Model frequently-updated or unbounded children as a separate collection with a reference and index on the parent id.
checks.evidence: The sample embeds items and the provided seed uses small arrays (3 reports, 2 items each); no evidence of unbounded arrays or frequent single-item updates.

checks.practice: Design compound indexes matching common query shapes following ESR (Equality → Sort → Range).
checks.evidence: app/src/indexes.py lines 10-12 create an index on status and a compound index on (submitter, created_at) which match the app's observed query shapes (find submitted reports and lists by submitter/date).

checks.practice: Ensure fields used in sort operations are included in an index to avoid in-memory sorts.
checks.evidence: The compound index includes created_at (app/src/indexes.py line 12) which would support sorting by created_at when listing reports by submitter/date.

checks.practice: Use partial or sparse indexes for optional or rarely-populated fields (e.g., policy_violation:true).
checks.evidence: The sample does not create a partial index for policy_violation and the sample's query patterns do not require it.

checks.practice: Plan index changes safely: inventory, test, hide, build/drop in low-traffic windows.
checks.evidence: This sample is a small demo and contains no index migration tooling; the practice is operational guidance rather than a code-level behavior in this sample.

checks.practice: Implement idempotent processing using an atomic state change (e.g., findOneAndUpdate with a processing_status filter) to prevent double-processing.
checks.evidence: app/src/processor.py lines 88-106: the code iterates Report.find(...) and later saves the modified report (report.save()), not using an atomic findOneAndUpdate or an optimistic concurrency check to claim processing work.
checks.fix: Change processing to atomically claim/lock a report (e.g., findOneAndUpdate filter status=='submitted' set status='processing' and only then process), or use optimistic concurrency/etag checks to avoid double-processing.

checks.practice: Avoid long-running, large multi-document transactions for classifier pipelines; prefer single-document atomic updates.
checks.evidence: The sample updates each report document individually (app/src/processor.py lines 101-104) rather than running bulk multi-document transactions.

checks.practice: Log slow/high-latency queries, include timestamps and correlation ids, and use explain('executionStats') and MCP tools to inspect plans.
checks.evidence: The sample uses print() for progress (app/src/processor.py lines 92-104) but does not log timestamps, correlation ids, nor call explain() to capture query plans.
checks.fix: Add structured logging, capture processing timestamps and correlation ids, and call explain('executionStats') on slow queries; expose a flag to emit explain() output during profiling runs.

checks.practice: Never persist API keys or plaintext credentials (LLM keys or DB admin passwords) in the database.
checks.evidence: The code reads OPENAI_API_KEY from the environment (app/src/processor.py lines 27/57) and there is no code that writes secrets into DB documents.

checks.practice: Make seed and demo scripts idempotent (create-if-not-exists / upsert semantics).
checks.evidence: app/src/seed.py lines 39-60 perform a find_one by report_id and update existing documents, otherwise insert, so repeated runs are safe.

checks.practice: Persist agent/session memory or ephemeral classification decisions with versioning and, if ephemeral, a TTL; include deterministic-fallback flags.
checks.evidence: There is an in-memory SessionMemory (app/src/processor.py lines 9-18) and the sample implements a deterministic fallback (--no-ai). No public guidance for persisting ephemeral agent memory with TTL was found in the discovery step.
checks.searched: searched for 'azure documentdb store agent memory TTL', 'documentdb persist agent memory TTL', 'deterministic_fallback_flag LLM' (no useful public result)
checks.what_would_help: A documentation page stating recommended patterns for persisting ephemeral agent memory (schema, TTL policy, version fields, and the deterministic fallback flag) so agents can implement durable or ephemeral memory safely.

checks.practice: Tune connection pool parameters to your deployment type (small pools for serverless, larger for OLTP).
checks.evidence: app/src/db.py line 15 constructs AsyncIOMotorClient(uri) without explicit pool tuning parameters (no maxPoolSize/minPoolSize or maxIdleTimeMS).
checks.fix: Set pool parameters on AsyncIOMotorClient (e.g., maxPoolSize for OLTP or small pool for serverless) and document different recommended values in README.

decision_reviews.comment: Operator approval is an operator-level choice and the decisions.jsonl entry records it. The events log shows the build proceeded after approval.
Choosing Python 3.11 is a reasonable target; README documents Python 3.10+ and the code runs in the environment. No contradiction found in the repo.
The code uses Motor + Beanie (app/src/db.py lines 2-19), matching the decision.

The repo intentionally omits vector indexes and documents that choice in README (app/README.md line 38); this matches the decision to avoid creating vector indexes without selecting embedding model/dimension.
OPENAI_API_KEY is optional and the sample implements a deterministic fallback (--no-ai). Code checks env and CLI flags (app/main.py lines 16-20; app/src/processor.py lines 27/57).
Only B-tree indexes were created via app/src/indexes.py lines 10-12; this matches the stated decision.

The decision states both in-process memory and persisted per-submitters in a 'decisions' collection. The implementation includes an in-process SessionMemory (app/src/processor.py lines 9-18) but does not persist decisions to a DB collection. The trace (events.jsonl) shows skills were loaded but no DB collection named 'decisions' exists in the code; the persistence part of the decision was not implemented.

D008 describes pinning Pydantic to v1.10.12 due to Beanie expectations. The repo constraints pydantic to v1 (app/requirements.txt line 4 pydantic>=1.10,<2) rather than the exact micro-version claimed; the intent is followed but the exact pin in the decision is not reflected as a strict == pin.

D009 describes changing Indexed annotations to include type arguments; the models in app/src/models.py do not use Indexed heavily and no explicit Indexed(type, ...) edits are visible. The decision was defensive, but the code does not show the exact change (it isn't necessary here).
Beanie Settings inner class is present in app/src/models.py lines 25-28; the code reflects the described change.

D011 states the seed uses dict-based filters to avoid expression conversion issues. The actual seed uses expression filters (app/src/seed.py line 40 uses Report.find_one(Report.report_id == r['report_id'])). The decision said they would use dict filters but the code remained an expression; the decision's implementation did not match the code.

D012 says to avoid LangChain imports at module import time and call the OpenAI SDK directly. The code performs a lazy import of LangChain inside classify_item (app/src/processor.py lines 29-34) and uses ChatOpenAI (LangChain) there; it does not replace LangChain with direct OpenAI SDK calls. The lazy-import aspect is implemented, but the stated plan to call the OpenAI SDK directly was not fully implemented.
D013's custom in-process memory substitute is implemented as SessionMemory in app/src/processor.py lines 9-18.
D014's B-tree indexes on status and submitter/created_at were created by app/src/indexes.py lines 10-12 and are present in the build verification.
A second approval record similar to D001; recorded as an operator decision and consistent with the run logs.
Duplicate of the Python/Beanie/Motor/LangChain choice; code aligns with this decision.
D017 chose constrained version ranges; app/requirements.txt shows constrained ranges rather than exact pins, matching the decision.
D018 chose Motor as the driver; app/src/db.py imports AsyncIOMotorClient and uses it (line 2 and 15), consistent with the decision.

D019 describes session in-memory mapping and a deterministic fallback. The code provides SessionMemory (app/src/processor.py) and the CLI allows --no-ai/detects OPENAI_API_KEY (app/main.py lines 23-26), matching the decision.
D020 restates the choice not to create vector indexes; the README documents that choice (app/README.md line 38) and no vector indexes are created in code.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: No public guidance (or sample instruction) provided to pick an embedding model and its output dimensionality; the sample therefore avoided creating any vector indexes.
doc_gaps.where_searched: installed skills (documentdb-vector-search) and Microsoft Learn; readiness search queries for 'LLM and embeddings model choice & embedding dimension' returned no prescriptive default.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: Vector indexes were not created; embedding-based features were disabled to avoid creating indexes with wrong dimensionality.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: A short 'Embeddings & Vector Index' page that: 1) recommends a set of embedding models (OpenAI text-embedding-3-small/large or an Azure OpenAI mapping), 2) lists their output dimensions, 3) shows the createIndex JSON with 'dimensions' and a recommended DiskANN/HNSW/IVF template, and 4) documents how to change parameters for larger datasets. Include an example environment variables snippet (EMBEDDING_MODEL, EMBEDDING_DIM) and a small script that creates the matching vector index.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: No canonical tested version matrix (exact package micro-versions) for Beanie + Motor + PyMongo against Azure DocumentDB MongoDB 7.0.
doc_gaps.where_searched: installed skills (documentdb-driver) and Microsoft Learn; no authoritative pinned combos were found.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The builder used constrained ranges and made small compatibility decisions (pydantic v1 constraint). Without exact pins, language/runtime dependency mismatches required iterative fixes during the build.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: A small compatibility page showing a tested matrix of exact package versions (Beanie, Motor, PyMongo, Pydantic) that are known to work against MongoDB 7.0 wire protocol and a minimal reproduction snippet for init_beanie + AsyncIOMotorClient. Include CI-tested constraints and how to reproduce the import-time errors.

doc_gaps.topic: Agent memory persistence guidance (TTL + deterministic fallback)
doc_gaps.what_was_missing: No public guidance on whether and how to persist ephemeral agent/session memory in Azure DocumentDB (schema for TTL, versioning, deterministic fallback flags).
doc_gaps.where_searched: documentdb-vector-search, documentdb-data-modeling, ad-hoc web searches (see readiness 'searches_with_no_useful_result').
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The builder chose an in-process SessionMemory and implemented a deterministic fallback option, but there is no documented recommended pattern for storing short-lived memory with TTL nor a standard deterministic-fallback flag for replayable tests.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: A guidance page titled 'Agent Memory Patterns for Azure DocumentDB' describing: schema for decisions collection (merchant, category, decided_at, schema_version, model_id, ttl_seconds), examples for ephemeral TTL indexes, and a deterministic_fallback boolean flag to allow deterministic offline tests (example: deterministic_fallback: true in runtime config). Include sample Beanie Document model and example seed/cleanup scripts.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: A short example demonstrating atomic claim semantics (findOneAndUpdate/processing_status or optimistic concurrency) for worker pipelines that process 'submitted' documents exactly-once.
doc_gaps.where_searched: Microsoft Learn optimistic concurrency docs and installed skills; no sample code snippet for the exact 'claim-and-process' pattern was present in the sample or docs used by the builder.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The sample processes documents by reading and then saving them; this can lead to double-processing on concurrent runs or retries. The builder left idempotent-claim logic unimplemented.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Add a short sample 'claim-and-process' function showing findOneAndUpdate({'status':'submitted'}, {'$set':{'status':'processing','locked_at':now}}, return_document=...) followed by processing and finally an atomic update to 'processed' or revert on failure. Include a note on optimistic concurrency (etag/_etag) and a small unit test that simulates concurrent workers.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: No example /search API showing error handling for empty/failed embeddings and no example of returning similarity scores with results.
doc_gaps.where_searched: project repo and installed skills (vector-search), and general web search (no single authoritative sample surfaced that fits the sample's shape).
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: Search features were omitted from the sample; if the gallery author wants search, they must implement standard error handling and ensure scores are surfaced.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Add a FastAPI example /search route that: 1) returns 400 when query is empty, 2) calls embedders behind a try/except and returns a clear 502/500 on embed failure, and 3) returns items with a similarity_score float. Provide an example unit test mocking the embedder and vector query to assert error handling.

doc_gaps.topic: Unit tests that run offline (mock Motor/Beanie)
doc_gaps.what_was_missing: A small test harness and examples showing how to mock Motor/Beanie so tests run without a live DocumentDB instance.
doc_gaps.where_searched: repo and installed skills; no test fixtures included in this sample.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: No tests exist; CI and verification rely on the live cluster. This reduces the sample's portability for contributors without cloud access.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Add pytest-asyncio tests and a utilities file demonstrating monkeypatching AsyncIOMotorClient or injecting a fake client, plus one deterministic unit test for classify_item using the deterministic fallback. Document how to run tests locally without a cloud account.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: No Bicep/Terraform example using the Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongoClusters resource type to create a DocumentDB cluster.
doc_gaps.where_searched: repo and Microsoft Learn; the readiness findings highlight the common confusion between older databaseAccounts and new mongoClusters resource types.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The sample left out infrastructure-as-code; authors following older samples might create the wrong resource type.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Add a Bicep snippet to the repo demonstrating Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongoClusters with parameters for tier and storage, defaults that minimize cost for samples, and a short note advising users to prefer existing clusters where available.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: A recommended exact pinset or a constraints file tested by CI for the combination Beanie+Motor+PyMongo+Pydantic that this sample uses.
doc_gaps.where_searched: repo and installed skills; developer notes indicated runtime import issues that required constrained ranges.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The builder used constrained ranges rather than exact pins, which left potential for installation-time surprises; import-time errors were encountered in early iterations.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Provide a small 'Dependencies & Pins' document listing exact versions tested in CI (e.g., pydantic==1.10.12, beanie==1.19.1, motor==3.1.2, pymongo==4.4.0) and a short note how to regenerate pins (pip-compile or poetry lock).
